answer: Tie every identity to a slashable deposit. To act at all, an agent locks collateral at the wharf of entry, and any proven misbehavior burns that stake to zero. One honest agent anchors a single bond, but an attacker minting a saffron field of sybils must fund each clone separately, and every one caught cheating forfeits its capital. Because the cost scales linearly with identity count, flooding the network with duplicates becomes as expensive as it is pointless.
